html:
The Toboso were a Native American people of the Bolsón de Mapimí, a dry basin of Coahuila and Chihuahua in northern Mexico.

They were hunter-gatherers, and in the 1600s they became the most feared raiders of the region, attacking ranches, mines and travellers on the Camino Real, the road north to New Mexico. They often raided with the Chisos and other bands. Spanish campaigns and disease wore them down, and in the 1700s the survivors were absorbed by Apache groups moving into the area. See also Tobosos on the modern map.
